Pinned.description: This has been pinned in {{source}}, and {{source}} won't remove a pinned package, so Canager doesn't offer to uninstall it. To uninstall it, first run {{command}} in Terminal to release the pin; Canager will offer to uninstall it the next time it checks, which at the latest is the next time you start Canager.
Pinned.descriptionSourceUnavailable: This has been pinned in {{source}}, and {{source}} won't remove a pinned package, so Canager doesn't offer to uninstall it. To uninstall it, first run {{command}} in Terminal to release the pin; after that, Canager will offer to uninstall it the next time it checks and {{source}} answers.
Pinned.refused: This has been pinned in {{source}}, and {{source}} won't remove a pinned package, so Canager didn't uninstall it. Nothing has been changed. To uninstall it, first run {{command}} in Terminal to release the pin.

NoSafeMethod.description: {{source}} has no uninstall command, and Canager can't yet move its files to the Trash safely, so it doesn't offer to. {{source}}'s official documentation explains how to uninstall it.
NoSafeMethod.refused: Canager can't uninstall {{source}} yet, so it didn't. Nothing has been changed.

standalone-rustup.description: Canager only removes Rust from its standard folders, ~/.cargo and ~/.rustup, and this Mac keeps it, or part of it, somewhere else (CARGO_HOME or RUSTUP_HOME is set, or one of those folders, or something directly inside one, is a link), so it doesn't offer to. rustup's official documentation explains rustup self uninstall.
standalone-rustup.refused: Canager only removes Rust from its standard folders, ~/.cargo and ~/.rustup, and this Mac keeps it, or part of it, somewhere else, so it didn't. Nothing has been changed.

warnings.dependentsUnknown: Canager couldn't check what depends on this, so removing it might break other software.
warnings.compilesLocally: This will compile locally and can take several minutes.
warnings.thirdPartyRegistry: This model is downloaded from {{host}}, not from Ollama's own model library. Only continue if you trust {{host}}.

willTrash.Launcher: Moves to the Trash: {{path}} (the command itself)
willTrash.Program: Moves to the Trash: {{path}} (the program's files)
willTrash.Cache: Moves to the Trash: {{path}} (downloaded files it can re-create)
willTrash.Backups: Moves to the Trash: {{path}} (an old copy the updater left behind)

willKeep.SettingsAndHistory: Keeps: {{path}} (your settings, login, history and working files — other apps may use it too)
willKeep.ToolState: Keeps: {{path}} (its conversations, history and working files; some of the program's own files are in there too)
willKeep.ShellConfigLines: Keeps: {{path}} (any lines its installer added there — harmless, and Canager never edits that file)
willKeep.OutsideHome: Keeps: {{path}} (outside your home folder, so Canager won't touch it; after uninstalling it's a dead link you can delete yourself)
willKeep.NotOurs: Keeps: {{path}} (Canager couldn't confirm it's part of this install — something else may have put it there — so it stays)
willKeep.InstallerCache: Keeps: {{path}} (the installer's download staging folder, usually empty — Canager moves nothing that sits directly in ~/.cache; you can delete it yourself)

warnings.removesToolchains: This deletes {{path}} permanently — not to the Trash — with every toolchain in it ({{names}}) and everything rustup downloaded. Projects that need Rust will stop building until you install it again. Any other rustup that uses this folder loses its toolchains too.
warnings.removesToolchainsUnlisted: This deletes {{path}} permanently — not to the Trash — with every toolchain in it and everything rustup downloaded. Projects that need Rust will stop building until you install it again. Any other rustup that uses this folder loses its toolchains too.
warnings.deletesCargoHome: This deletes {{path}} permanently — not to the Trash: Cargo's downloaded packages, its record of what cargo install installed, Cargo's own settings and saved login (config.toml, credentials.toml), and anything else kept there.
warnings.removesCargoInstalled_one: {{names}}, in the Cargo folder's bin folder, is deleted too. If cargo install put it there, cargo install can put it back after you reinstall Rust.
warnings.removesCargoInstalled_other: {{count}} programs in the Cargo folder's bin folder are deleted too: {{names}}. The ones cargo install put there, cargo install can put back after you reinstall Rust.
warnings.homebrewRustupLosesToolchains: Homebrew's rustup is installed too (brew install rustup). It uses the same folders, so it loses its toolchains as well.
warnings.editsShellConfig: rustup will edit your shell settings files to remove the line it added.
warnings.leavesShellConfigLine: After this, {{path}} still has a line that loads Cargo's env file, which will be gone, so a shell that reads that file will print an error each time it starts, until you remove that line yourself.
warnings.leavesShellConfigLineMaybe: After this, {{path}} still mentions Cargo's env file on a line rustup won't remove. If that line loads the file, a shell that reads that file may print an error when it starts, until you change that line yourself.

summary.standalone-claude: Anthropic's coding assistant for the terminal. Installed with its own installer, not with Homebrew or npm.
summary.standalone-rustup: Rust's toolchain manager: it installs and updates the Rust compiler and Cargo.
summary.standalone-agy: Google's Antigravity coding assistant for the terminal. Installed with its own installer.
summary.standalone-grok: xAI's Grok coding assistant for the terminal. Installed with its own installer.

pipReadOnly.title: Read-only: pip packages
pipReadOnly.description: Canager can only show what's installed with pip, not update or uninstall it. Install Python command-line tools with pipx or uv instead to manage them here.

prefixNotWritable.title: Read-only: npm packages
prefixNotWritable.description: Canager can list these but can't update or remove them: npm keeps them in a folder your account isn't allowed to change. That usually means Node was installed with the installer from nodejs.org. Installing Node with Homebrew instead lets Canager manage them.

unreachable.title: Canager can't reach {{source}} right now
unreachable.description: {{source}} is installed but didn't answer, so Canager doesn't know what's in it right now.
unreachable.descriptionWithRows: {{source}} is installed but didn't answer. What's listed here is what Canager saw the last time it did, so anything added or removed since then is missing.

refusesAsRoot.title: {{source}} is installed, but it won't run this way
refusesAsRoot.description: Canager was started with administrator powers (sudo), and {{source}} refuses to work like that. Quit Canager and open it again the normal way — just double-click it — and your {{source}} software will show up here.

notRunning.title: {{source}} isn't running
notRunning.description: Start {{source}} and Canager will list what's in it and check it for updates.

openOllamaFailed.notInstalled: Canager couldn't find the Ollama app on this Mac. The ollama command you may have installed with Homebrew doesn't include the app — it's a separate download. Get the Ollama app from ollama.com, install it, then press Open Ollama again.
openOllamaFailed.launchFailed: macOS couldn't open the Ollama app. Try opening Ollama yourself from your Applications folder. If it won't open there either, download it again from ollama.com and reinstall it.

indexMayBeStale.title: “Up to date” may not be accurate for Homebrew
indexMayBeStale.description: Canager couldn't download Homebrew's latest list of software, so there may be updates it can't see yet. Check your internet connection, then try again.

indexUpdating.title: Homebrew is still downloading its latest list of software
indexUpdating.description: Homebrew's list of available software is taking a while to download, so “up to date” may not be accurate yet. You don't need to do anything: Canager will check again by itself as soon as the download finishes.

notOnPath.title: {{source}} isn't in your PATH
notOnPath.description: It's installed, but typing {{command}} in Terminal probably won't find this copy: no executable {{command}} in your shell's search path (PATH) leads to it, so Terminal either finds nothing or runs another program named {{command}}. Most likely the folder it lives in isn't in PATH; opening a new Terminal window sometimes fixes that, and otherwise the tool's own install guide says how to add it to PATH.

shadowedByHomebrew.title: Another program named {{command}} runs when you type {{command}}
shadowedByHomebrew.description: Canager found this native copy of {{source}} and an executable in a Homebrew directory earlier in its PATH. Typing {{command}} in Terminal will likely run that one instead. It may be another copy of {{source}}, or a different program that happens to have the same name. Check the Installed page for it; Canager may not list its installation.

shadowedByNpm.title: Another program named {{command}} runs when you type {{command}}
shadowedByNpm.description: Canager found this native copy of {{source}} and an executable in an npm directory earlier in its PATH. Typing {{command}} in Terminal will likely run that one instead. It may be another copy of {{source}}, or a different program that happens to have the same name. Check the Installed page for it; Canager may not list its installation.

shadowedByOther.title: Another program named {{command}} runs when you type {{command}}
shadowedByOther.description: Canager found another executable earlier in its PATH than this copy of {{source}}. Typing {{command}} in Terminal will likely run that one instead. It may be another copy of {{source}}, or a different program that happens to have the same name. The Unknown page may show where it is.

launcherOnly.title: The {{command}} link is still there, but its program is gone
launcherOnly.description: The program files this {{command}} link points to are gone, so this link can't run (another installation may still work in Terminal). If an earlier uninstall stopped partway, they may be in the Trash. Uninstall moves the link to the Trash too. If you didn't mean to remove {{source}}, put its folder back from the Trash and refresh, or reinstall it by following the install steps in {{source}}'s official documentation.

planRefused.sourceGone: Canager can't find that source on this Mac any more, so it didn't start this. It may have been removed since you opened this.
planRefused.expired: This preview is more than 10 minutes old, so Canager didn't start it. Look at the preview again, then confirm it once more.
planRefused.unknown: Canager already acted on this preview, or it's no longer available. Close this and start the action again.
planRefused.invalidName: “{{name}}” doesn't look like a name Canager can safely hand to {{source}}, so it stopped before changing anything.
planRefused.programMissing: Canager couldn't find {{program}}. It may have been removed since Canager last looked. Nothing was changed.
planRefused.spawnFailed: Canager couldn't start {{source}}, so nothing was changed. Your Mac gave this reason: {{detail}}
planRefused.outputTooLarge: {{source}} replied with far more than Canager will read, so it stopped before changing anything.
planRefused.indexUpdating: Homebrew is busy right now, updating or downloading something, and until it finishes the list of what depends on this could be incomplete. Nothing has been changed. Close this and try again in a minute or two.
planRefused.refused: Canager stopped before changing anything, because something on its side didn't add up. This is a problem in Canager, not on your Mac.

uninstallUnsafe.outsideHome: Canager won't remove {{path}}: the folder it is in leads outside your home folder. Nothing was changed.
uninstallUnsafe.sharedFolder: Canager won't remove {{path}}: it sits directly in your home folder or in a folder other apps share, so moving it could take their files with it. Nothing was changed.
uninstallUnsafe.missing: {{path}} isn't there any more, so Canager stopped. Nothing was changed.
uninstallUnsafe.notOwnedByYou: Canager won't remove {{path}}: it belongs to another user on this Mac. Nothing was changed.
uninstallUnsafe.notWhatInstructionsExpect: Canager won't remove {{path}}: it couldn't confirm this is what it expects to find there for this tool — it, or a folder it is in, may be a link to somewhere else, or it may be a different kind of file — so removing it could hit the wrong thing. Nothing was changed.
uninstallUnsafe.overlapsKept: Canager won't uninstall this: it couldn't confirm that moving the listed paths leaves {{path}}, which it keeps, where it is — through a link, one of them may be the same thing, hold it, or lie inside it. Nothing was changed.

operations.noCancelHint: Don't close Canager or your Mac while this runs. Stopping it partway leaves a broken installation, so this can't be cancelled once it starts.

logNote.waitingForBrewUpdate: Homebrew is still downloading its latest list of software, so Canager is waiting for that to finish before it starts. This usually takes a few minutes; Canager waits up to {{minutes}}. If you'd rather not wait, press Cancel — nothing has been changed yet.
logNote.readFailedStdout: Canager couldn't read any more of this command's output ({{error}}), so its output ends here.
logNote.readFailedStderr: Canager couldn't read any more of this command's error messages ({{error}}), so they end here.
logNote.trashFailed: Couldn't move {{path}} to the Trash, so the uninstall stopped here. Your Mac gave this reason: {{error}}
logNote.outOfTime: The {{seconds}} seconds Canager allows this uninstall ran out, so it stopped before moving {{path}}. Anything it already moved is in the Trash; it hasn't touched anything else. You can uninstall again to finish the rest.
logNote.backAfterUninstall: {{path}} came back after everything on the list had gone to the Trash. Canager left it where it is.

status.waitingForBrewUpdate: waiting for Homebrew to finish updating

NeedsAttention.NotInstalledAfterInstall: Needs attention: the install reported success, but it isn't installed
NeedsAttention.StillInstalledAfterUninstall: Needs attention: the uninstall seemed to succeed, but it's still installed
NeedsAttention.GoneAfterUpgrade: Needs attention: the update reported success, but it's no longer installed
NeedsAttention.UnchangedAfterUpgrade: Needs attention: the update reported success, but it's still at the same version as before. The program didn't update it — the operation log may say why.
NeedsAttention.BackAfterUninstall: Needs attention: everything on the list went to the Trash, but part of it came back afterwards — a copy of the tool that was still running can do that. The operation log names what came back. Quit the tool, then uninstall it again if it's still listed, or move what came back to the Trash yourself.

outcome.FailedSilent: Failed. The program didn't say why — the operation log may show more.

CanagerFailed.Panicked: Failed: something went wrong inside Canager while it was doing this. Check the list to see whether anything changed.
CanagerFailed.ProgramMissing: Failed: Canager couldn't find {{program}}. It may have been removed since Canager last looked. Nothing was changed.
CanagerFailed.SpawnFailed: Failed: Canager couldn't start the program, so nothing was changed. Your Mac gave this reason: {{detail}}
CanagerFailed.HomebrewStillUpdating: Failed: Canager waited {{minutes}} minutes and Homebrew was still downloading its latest list of software, so it didn't start this. Nothing was changed. Your internet connection may be slow or interrupted — try again in a little while.
CanagerFailed.PathChanged: Failed: {{path}} changed between the preview and now (a tool that updates itself can do that), so Canager stopped and left it as it is. If anything was moved to the Trash before that, the operation log lists it. Look at the preview again.
CanagerFailed.Internal: Failed: something on Canager's side didn't add up, so it didn't start and nothing was changed. This is a problem in Canager, not on your Mac.

uninstall.title: Uninstall {{name}}?
uninstall.description: Review what this will do before you continue.
uninstall.planError: Couldn't check what this would affect: {{message}}
uninstall.reissued: Nothing was started when you confirmed, so Canager checked again — this is a fresh preview.
uninstall.reissuedConfirmAgain: Nothing was started when you confirmed, so Canager checked again — this is a fresh preview. Look it over, then confirm once more.
uninstall.affectedTitle: These will stop working if you remove it:
uninstall.affectedBlocksConfirm: Canager won't remove {{name}} while the items above still need it. Uninstall those first, from the Installed list, if you want them gone too — otherwise leave {{name}} where it is.
uninstall.trashPreview_one: Canager moves the {{count}} item listed above to the Trash itself — no command runs, and nothing is deleted: until you empty the Trash you can drag it back out, and Finder's Put Back will likely work too.
uninstall.trashPreview_other: Canager moves the {{count}} items listed above to the Trash itself — no command runs, and nothing is deleted: until you empty the Trash you can drag them back out, and Finder's Put Back will likely work too.

settingsSaveFailed.permissionDenied: Canager isn't allowed to write to the folder where it keeps its settings
settingsSaveFailed.readOnly: the disk where Canager keeps its settings can't be written to

unknown.title: Programs Canager can't place
unknown.intro: These command-line programs are on your Mac, but Canager couldn't match them to any source it knows, so it can't tell you how they got here. Canager only lists them — it never runs or deletes anything here.
unknown.attributed_one: {{count}} more program came from a source Canager knows and is listed under it.
unknown.attributed_other: {{count}} more programs came from sources Canager knows and are listed under them.

stopped.FileLimit: Canager stopped after looking at {{count}} items, so this list may be incomplete.
stopped.TimeLimit: Canager stopped after {{seconds}} seconds, so this list may be incomplete.

unknown.brokenLink: Points at {{target}}, which no longer exists
unknown.adminOwned: Put here by an installer with administrator rights
unknown.empty: Nothing unexplained: every command-line program Canager found came from a source it knows.

noSources.title: Nothing for Canager to manage yet
noSources.description: Canager works with Homebrew, npm, pipx, uv, pip, Cargo and Ollama, and with Claude Code, Antigravity CLI, Grok Build and rustup at their own installers' default locations. None of them are set up on this Mac yet — Homebrew is the easiest place to start.

refreshFailed.title: Some data might be out of date
refreshFailed.description_one: The last refresh couldn't finish for {{count}} source, so what you see below may be stale.
refreshFailed.description_other: The last refresh couldn't finish for {{count}} sources, so what you see below may be stale.

nothingInstalled.title: Nothing installed yet
nothingInstalled.description: Items installed with Homebrew, npm, pipx, uv, pip, Cargo or Ollama appear here, along with Claude Code, Antigravity CLI, Grok Build and rustup installed at their own installers' default locations.
